I looked at the file and the statement, and I'm not going to be able to prove it here.

The theorem says that a graded quotient `R` of `k[x_0,…,x_n]` is Cohen–Macaulay if and only if its localization at the irrelevant ideal is. Proving that needs a substantial body of commutative algebra: depth, Ext-based characterizations of Cohen–Macaulay, and the graded-to-local comparison. Mathlib here has no usable version of that theory, and the definitions in the file (depth as a supremum over Ext vanishing, Cohen–Macaulay defined through `ringKrullDim` equalling depth) don't reduce to anything simpler. I also checked whether the defined classes collapse to something trivially provable, and they don't. The file still compiles with the single `sorry` warning and I have not modified it.

I give up.
